starting_worktree.origin: FW-AUTHORITY-EXPIRY-ENFORCEMENT-001's delta, pre-existing for this mission
pre-existing, contains four earlier missions' receipts

existing_identity_primitives_found.request_id: RemoteCapabilityRequest.request_id: str -- generated ONCE by the SENDER, before any transfer/transport step, via fi._new_id('CAPREQ') = envelope.validate_mission_id(f'CAPREQ-{uuid4().hex}'). Never regenerated by receiver or transport. Passed through fabric.loopback.wire's JSON serialization verbatim (confirmed: capability_request_to_wire()/safe_capability_request_from_wire() copy request_id field-for-field, no transformation) -- the natural, already-stable candidate identity for a logical request.
existing_identity_primitives_found.correlation_id / causation_id: correlation_id threads a TransferRequest through to its RemoteCapabilityRequest and response; causation_id on a RemoteCapabilityResult/FabricReceipt = the causing request_id. Both are derived/copied FROM request_id-bearing objects, not independent identities -- request_id remains the root identity.
existing_identity_primitives_found.artifact_id: identifies the ARTIFACT, not the request. FabricArtifactIndex is keyed by artifact_id; two independent capability requests can legitimately share one artifact_id (proven by the existing, unmodified test test_identical_resubmission_is_not_a_conflict) and must both execute -- artifact_id is the wrong key for request-level replay detection.
existing_identity_primitives_found.receipt_id: compute_receipt_id() is a deterministic function of (correlation_id, causation_id=request_id, source, dest, artifact_id, sha256, capability_id, transfer_state, capability_status) -- reproducible, but computed AFTER the fact from a rendered disposition, not usable as a pre-execution replay key without already knowing the outcome.

existing_dedup_primitives_found.FabricArtifactIndex.check_and_record(): in-memory, keyed by artifact_id, rejects a DIFFERENT sha256 under an already-seen artifact_id (CAP_DUPLICATE_CONFLICT). Does NOT reject or recognize an identical resubmission -- confirmed by the existing, unmodified, still-passing test test_identical_resubmission_is_not_a_conflict, which asserts BOTH of two capability requests for the same artifact_id+sha256 return CAP_COMPLETED. This is a content-identity conflict detector, not a request-replay guard, and this mission does not change it.
existing_dedup_primitives_found.LineageStore.record(): durable, JSONL, file-locked, keyed by artifact_id. Identical re-recording of the same artifact_id's manifest is an idempotent no-op (raises LineageConflictError on differing content) -- but this dedupes the MANIFEST WRITE only. Confirmed by direct code trace: process_remote_capability_request() calls ah_interface.handoff() (which writes to LineageStore) immediately before provider.invoke() runs, on EVERY successful-authority path, regardless of whether that exact artifact_id was already handed off before. It does not gate provider.invoke() at all.
existing_dedup_primitives_found.conclusion: TWO IDENTICAL capability requests differing only by a fresh request_id (a genuinely new logical request re-using old content) legitimately execute twice today -- correct existing behavior (TEST 7 preserves this). TWO capability requests sharing the SAME request_id (a literal message replay) ALSO executed twice before this mission, in-process, with NOTHING recognizing them as the same logical request -- this is the confirmed gap this mission closes. The only accidental partial mitigation found: InMemoryFabricTransport.pull() is destructive (empties the inbox), so a naive exact-replay whose envelope was already consumed on the first delivery would incidentally hit 'no envelope waiting' (CAP_FAILED) on a second delivery -- but this is fragile (depends entirely on transport/envelope timing, not request identity), dishonest (misreports a true duplicate as a data-availability failure rather than returning the real original disposition), and was proven as an explicit regression-guard test in this mission (fabric/tests/test_message_identity_replay.py::TestReplayGuardOmittedPreservesPriorBehavior) rather than relied upon.

chosen_request_identity: RemoteCapabilityRequest.request_id (no new field introduced; the existing sender-generated identifier is reused exactly as the mission's Section 6 requires when a suitable one already exists).
identity_generation_boundary: sender, at RemoteCapabilityRequest construction time, before any transfer/transport step. Never regenerated by transport or receiver.
identity_persistence: Durable, on disk, per receiving node: fabric.interface.RequestReplayGuard writes one JSONL ledger (request_dispositions.jsonl) plus one lock file (request_dispositions.lock) under the SAME --lineage-dir both pc_node_server.py scripts already accept and pass to LineageStore -- no new CLI plumbing, no new directory convention.
replay_store: fabric.interface.RequestReplayGuard -- a NEW class, but reusing evidence_envelope.envelope's exact existing durability primitives (_FileLock, _atomic_write_bytes, _serialize_ledger, LedgerIntegrityError) that artifact_handoff.lineage_store.LineageStore and evidence_envelope's own TrajectoryStore already build on. This is the fourth application of that identical discipline in this repository, not a new persistence technology (architecture/authority-map.md's own prior 'duplicate_or_parallel_implementations' note already names this pattern as deliberate reuse, not accidental duplication).
replay_check_location: The very first statement inside process_remote_capability_request(), before transport.pull() is ever called -- a replayed request_id short-circuits before touching the transport's inbox, the artifact-hash validation, or FabricArtifactIndex, and returns the ORIGINAL recorded disposition without re-deriving anything.
authority_check_location: Unchanged position (after envelope pull/hash-validate/artifact-index-check, before capability lookup) -- reached ONLY on a request_id never seen before by replay_guard. A replay never reaches this line at all, which is what guarantees a duplicate can neither gain nor lose authority relative to its first delivery.
execution_boundary: provider.invoke() -- unchanged call site. Now additionally gated by: request_id not previously recorded (replay_guard) AND authority_permits() True AND provider registered. A resolved disposition (CAP_UNAUTHORIZED, CAP_UNSUPPORTED, CAP_FAILED, CAP_INCOMPLETE, or the provider's real status) is durably recorded via a new _finalize() closure immediately after being computed, before returning to the caller.

crash_windows.A_request_received_identity_persisted_cr: Does not apply to this implementation: RequestReplayGuard never records a disposition BEFORE authority is evaluated and (if authorized) the capability is invoked -- recording happens strictly AFTER provider.invoke() returns (or after an equivalent post-authority decision like CAP_UNAUTHORIZED/CAP_UNSUPPORTED). There is no window where an identity is durably marked 'seen' before its outcome is known, so a crash in this window simply means nothing was recorded and the request remains fully retriable from scratch -- the safest possible outcome, not a gap.
crash_windows.B_execution_occurs_crash_before_completi: A REAL, UNRESOLVED risk: provider.invoke() returning successfully and the process crashing before RequestReplayGuard.record_once() durably writes the disposition would mean a subsequent replay is NOT recognized and the capability executes a SECOND time. This mission's implementation does not close this window -- doing so would require making capability invocation and disposition recording a single atomic step, which content_read and other providers do not support today (invoke() is a plain function call, not a two-phase commit). Recorded here as an explicit, unresolved crash window, per Section 8's instruction not to hide it.
crash_windows.C_completion_persisted_response_lost_sen: FULLY HANDLED and tested (TestRetryAfterLostResponseGetsOriginalDisposition / TEST 6): once record_once() returns, any later delivery of the same request_id gets the TRUE original disposition back, never a fresh execution and never a misleading failure.

production_files_changed.change: added CAP_DUPLICATE_COMPLETED/CAP_DUPLICATE_DENIED to _CAP_STATES; added RequestReplayConflictError and RequestReplayGuard classes (reusing evidence_envelope.envelope's durability primitives); added optional replay_guard parameter to process_remote_capability_request(), a replay short-circuit at function entry, and a _finalize() closure that records post-authority dispositions and converts the six existing post-authority _result_and_receipt() call sites to route through it. Added 'import json'. No existing function signature's REQUIRED parameters changed; replay_guard defaults to None and is fully backward compatible (proven by TestReplayGuardOmittedPreservesPriorBehavior).
constructs replay_guard = fi.RequestReplayGuard(Path(lineage_dir)) in run_server(); threads it through _handle_capability_request() into process_remote_capability_request(). 3 lines changed.

first_delivery_result: CAP_COMPLETED, executor invoked exactly once (proven in-process and over both transports).
duplicate_delivery_result: CAP_DUPLICATE_COMPLETED (when the original disposition was CAP_COMPLETED) or CAP_DUPLICATE_DENIED (any other original disposition, e.g. CAP_UNAUTHORIZED) -- structured_result on a CAP_DUPLICATE_COMPLETED reply is byte-identical to the original.
duplicate_execution_count: 0 in every test across all three layers (in-process, loopback subprocess, TCP subprocess) and across a real two-process restart -- proven via spy invocation_count (in-process) and via the durable LineageStore record count staying at exactly 1 after two deliveries (transport tests), since ah_interface.handoff() -- which writes the lineage record -- is never reached on a replayed request_id.
loopback_result: 8/8 authority-expiry-transport tests (unchanged) + 2/2 new replay tests pass: TEST 4 (same request_id sent twice over one real AF_UNIX connection executes once) and TEST 9 (a genuinely separate second OS subprocess, reading the same on-disk --lineage-dir a terminated first server wrote to, still recognizes the duplicate and returns CAP_DUPLICATE_COMPLETED without any envelope present in its own fresh in-memory transport).
tcp_result: 5/5 authority-expiry-transport tests (unchanged) + 2/2 new replay tests pass, identical proof over 127.0.0.1 with an OS-assigned ephemeral port, real process restart included.
restart_result: PROVEN with a REAL second OS subprocess (not simulated in-process only) for both transports: server 1 executes and terminates cleanly (SHUTDOWN + clean process exit, returncode 0), server 2 is spawned fresh pointing at the identical --lineage-dir, and correctly returns CAP_DUPLICATE_COMPLETED for the replayed request_id purely from the durable ledger -- server 2's own transport inbox is empty and never touched, since the replay check short-circuits before transport.pull().
authority_invariants_preserved: TestReplayNeverWeakensADenial proves a request denied (CAP_UNAUTHORIZED) on first delivery stays denied (CAP_DUPLICATE_DENIED) on replay even when the replayed message carries a NOW-VALID authority_context -- a duplicate cannot gain authority. TestExpiredDuplicateNeverExecutes proves the converse: a request completed while authority was valid, replayed under an EXPIRED authority_context, still returns CAP_DUPLICATE_COMPLETED without re-invoking the capability or re-evaluating the now-expired grant -- a duplicate cannot lose or gain authority by being re-evaluated at all. All FW-AUTHORITY-EXPIRY-* suites (authority_permits() unit tests, in-process E2E, loopback transport, TCP transport -- 35 tests total) re-run unchanged and pass.

counterevidence: None found against the implemented invariant. One pre-existing, still-correct behavior was explicitly re-verified rather than disturbed: two independent capability requests sharing an artifact_id but carrying distinct request_ids both execute (test_identical_resubmission_is_not_a_conflict, unmodified, still passing, and re-demonstrated by this mission's own TEST 7).
limitations: Crash window B (capability executes, process crashes before the disposition is durably recorded) is NOT closed by this implementation -- explicitly recorded above, not hidden. Closing it would require atomic invoke+record semantics that no current provider supports.

replay_guard is opt-in (defaults to None) at the process_remote_capability_request() API level. Only fabric/loopback/pc_node_server.py and fabric/tcp/pc_node_server.py were wired to supply it; any other future caller of process_remote_capability_request() that omits replay_guard gets zero replay protection, silently, by design (matching the existing optional lineage_store/artifact_index pattern) -- this is a deliberate default, not an oversight, but worth flagging for any future caller audit.

RequestReplayGuard.record_once()'s check-then-act sequence is not wrapped in the same file lock as the read+compare+write (the read happens once at function entry via .get(), a second read+compare+write happens later inside record_once() itself under its own lock) -- safe for this architecture's actual concurrency model (each spawned server processes one connection, one message at a time, strictly sequentially; proven empirically by every test in this mission), but would need a single lock spanning both the early check and the final record if a future multi-threaded or multi-connection receiver were introduced. Recorded as a scope boundary, not a present defect.

This mission's replay window is bounded by --lineage-dir's lifetime (an operator-managed directory, never auto-pruned). No retention/expiry policy for request_dispositions.jsonl exists; an operationally long-lived PC_NODE would accumulate one record per ever-seen request_id indefinitely. Out of scope for this mission (no such policy exists for LineageStore's own artifact_lineage.jsonl either, matching precedent).

resulting_capability_claim.claim: LOCAL_CAPABILITY_REQUEST_REPLAY_SUPPRESSION_PROVEN -- within the tested local ForgeWorld substrate (in-process, AF_UNIX loopback subprocess, and localhost AF_INET TCP subprocess, including across a real second-process restart reading the same durable ledger), a capability request identified by its sender-generated request_id executes its registered capability at most once: a first delivery executes and durably records its disposition; any later delivery of the identical request_id -- immediate, wire-roundtripped, or after a real process restart -- returns that same original disposition without re-invoking the capability, and does so without re-deriving or weakening the authority decision (a duplicate can neither gain authority, per TestReplayNeverWeakensADenial, nor lose it, per TestExpiredDuplicateNeverExecutes).
explicitly_not_claimed: exactly-once distributed execution (crash window B is open and disclosed)
network security / message integrity / peer authentication (deliberately deferred to later layers per Section 14)
protection against a receiver process crashing between successful invocation and disposition persistence
